claims.text: Machine-learning models trained on HEA processing data can identify an optimal severe-plastic-deformation and aging regime.
Severe plastic deformation followed by tailored aging will produce a hierarchical or duplex microstructure in HEAs.
The resulting microstructure will contain both nanoscale or ultrafine grains and controlled precipitates.
The hierarchical microstructure will promote beneficial dislocation interactions and twinning.
The proposed microstructure will minimize excessive residual stress.
Severe plastic deformation generates a high density of grain boundaries and defects that act as nucleation sites.
Controlled aging refines and stabilizes precipitates and lamellar features.
The combined processing route will improve load transfer.
The combined processing route will restrict shear localization.
Balancing the operative deformation mechanisms will reduce the strength–ductility trade-off.
The optimized treatment will increase yield and tensile strengths relative to conventional casting and annealing.
The strength improvement will exceed 10%.
The optimized treatment will maintain or improve ductility relative to conventional processing.
The optimized treatment will enhance Young's modulus.
The optimized treatment will increase resistance to crack initiation and fracture toughness.
The method is expected to work for HEAs that are sensitive to processing-induced microstructural refinement.
Performance improvements may fail for compositions or processing regimes outside the machine-learning model's validated training domain.
Overly aggressive severe plastic deformation may create residual stresses that trigger brittle behavior.
Conventionally cast and annealed HEAs typically exhibit strength–ductility trade-offs and limited fracture-resistance enhancement.
CrCoNi-based HEA/MEAs can obtain high toughness and damage tolerance through sustained strain hardening involving twinning and transformation-induced plasticity.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis says all four properties will be enhanced, while the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained; the falsification rule again requires statistically significant improvement across all metrics.
